context p95 28,576 ms (p50 9,328 ms) at 500,000 tables misses the 200 ms target. Profiled at this size, 87% of a context call is the join-path search's exact A* lower bound: a reverse Dijkstra over every table within the 6-hop limit of the target(s), about 1 s each, ~18 per question (graph expansion's multi-seed searches 62% of the time, the hazard scan over every candidate pair 34%). In the synthetic catalog one join component holds ~450,000 tables, so that 6-hop ball is a large share of the catalog. Within the architecture the bound now stops at the hop limit and context reads only the joins in scope (2,000 tables: p95 259 -> 119 ms; 20,000 tables: p50 3.9 -> 1.0 s, p95 5.3 -> 1.5 s); meeting the target needs an architecture change (precomputed distance bounds such as landmarks, or a hazard scan that does not search every candidate pair), reported for the release notes
join-path search p95 1,222 ms at 500,000 tables (no fixed target; regression-gated): the same per-target lower bound, plus the fewest-hops walk that words a NO_ROUTE explanation
